The '''Y'bith''', also known as "'''Ghost Bith'''," were a [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]] of the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]]. The ancestors of the Y'bith were Bith who occupied the domed [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Nozho/Legends|Nozho]] on [[Clak'dor VII/Legends|Clak'dor VII]], but a [[Nozho–Weogar War/Legends|civil war]] between that city and the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]], [[Weogar/Legends|Weogar]], would inadvertently create the subspecies. Weogar launched a biological attack against Nozho, destroying most of the wildlife and killing many of the citizens. Those who survived suffered from [[Mutant|mutagenic]] irregularities, leading them to be branded as "Ghost Bith." The Y'bith eventually left what remained of Nozho, and relocated to [[Clak'dor IV]].

Bioengineers were able to stabilize the mutation of the Y'bith, but the beings took some [[Time/Legends|time]] to adapt to their newfound genetic features. Developing their own culture, the Y'bith were never fully embraced by the Bith, who cited the volatile biochemistry of the subspecies which made them violent and aggressive. Nevertheless, the Y'bith strove to be accepted by the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] community as a whole, and their city of [[New Nozho]] became a notable trade port. The Y'bith also aided in the rebuilding efforts that took place in the wake of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].

==Biology and appearance==
The physical features that were unique to the Y'bith and not possessed by the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] themselves were a direct result of the biological attack on the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Nozho/Legends|Nozho]]. The Y'bith featured [[Color/Legends|orange]], sensitive skin, poor [[Eye/Legends|eyesight]], strong [[Limb/Legends|hands]] and feet, thicker [[Bone/Legends|bones]], and ductile [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] structures. In addition to that, they possessed volatile biochemistry, making them prone to violence and aggression.<ref name="db" />

==Society and culture==
The Y'bith always strove to be accepted by their Bith cousins, even when faced with harsh refusal. As a whole, they resolved to not be satisfied with anything but acceptance from the Bith. They saw their story as one of success, and hoped that [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as a whole would agree with their point of view. As a result, the Y'bith were constantly trying to prove themselves as a people.<ref name="db" />

==History==
[[File:ClakdorVII.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Clak'dor VII, the location of the war]]
At some stage in the early history of the Bith, a bitter rivalry brewed between two prominent cities on [[Clak'dor VII/Legends|Clak'dor VII]]: the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] city [[Weogar/Legends|Weogar]], and the domed city of Nozho. In approximately [[300 BBY/Legends|300 BBY]],<ref name="TEGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> relations between the two cities broke down over a dispute pertaining to a [[Sublight engine/Legends|stardrive]] patent. As a result, the [[Nozho–Weogar War/Legends|Nozho-Weogar War]] broke out, causing insurmountable damage to the biosphere of [[Clak'dor VII/Legends|Clak'dor VII]]. During the war, Weogar launched a biological attack against Nozho, effectively destroying the city, as well as causing [[Mutant|mutations]] in both the populace and the nearby wildlife. Those surviving Bith that had suffered mutations were in a minority, though; most of Nozho's populace had been killed in the attack. The irregularities that were a result of the mutations were consistent amongst all the survivors, leading to the creation of what was essentially a [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]] of the Bith.<ref name="db" />

In the wake of the devastating attack, the survivors, dubbed "Y'bith," or, in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], "Ghost Bith,"<ref name="db" /> lived in domed,<ref name="negtas">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> hermetically sealed cities that had been built in the ruins of Nozho. In time, they departed the ruins, and Clak'dor VII altogether, instead choosing to settle on the world of [[Clak'dor IV]]. There, the Y'bith established the city of [[New Nozho]]. While the bioengineers amongst the Y'bith were able to stabilize the mutation, the populace found it difficult to adapt to their new physical features and traits. The Y'bith were tolerated by the Bith, but they were never openly embraced by them. Although some would claim that the Bith's reluctance to accept the Y'bith was borne from guilt over the Nozho attacks, the Bith themselves denied the accusation. They instead cited the volatile biochemistry of the Y'bith as their reason for apprehension. Nevertheless, the Y'bith strove for acceptance not just from the Bith, but from the wider galactic community. New Nozho itself would eventually become a thriving trade port.<ref name="db" />

==Y'bith in the galaxy==
As they were constantly striving for acceptance from the galactic community, the Y'bith spread to [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] other than Clak'dor IV. As a result, they formed notable minority presences on worlds, such as [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], and the galactic capital, [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="db" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Graven R'ube]], a member of the race, was present at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Cantina]]<ref name="hs">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].<ref name="SWB">{{SW|url=news/the-star-wars-holiday-special-cantina-we-may-not-thrive-friend-but-we-survive-friend|text=''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' Cantina: Who's Who|int=The Star Wars Holiday Special Cantina: Who's Who|nolive=1}}</ref> Later, on both Nar Shaddaa and Coruscant, they aided in the rebuilding efforts in the wake of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="db" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:NearBith.jpg|thumb|left|A Y'bith in ''Star Wars: Yoda Stories''.]]
The [[Species/Legends|species]] of the Y'bith first appeared, albeit unidentified, in [[1978]]'s ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''.<ref name="hs" /> They would go unused for several decades, save for scant appearances in the non-[[canon]] computer [[Star Wars video games|game]] ''[[Star Wars: Yoda Stories]]'', where they were used as generic non-player characters.<ref name="ys">''[[Star Wars: Yoda Stories]]''</ref> In [[2006]], the species was identified and fleshed out by [[Evan Burger]]&mdash;writing as "ShadowCultist"&mdash;through the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature "[[What's The Story?]]" Burger, noting the visual similarity between the species and the Bith, decided to make them a mutant offshoot of the latter, and in doing so based their name, "Y'bith," on the original. Looking for a way to explain the mutation, Burger searched [[Wookieepedia]] for a suitable catalyst. He found one in the Nozho-Weogar War,<ref name="blog">{{Blog|SWB01|1|Y'bith: Behind the Scenes}}</ref> which had originated in [[Troy Denning]]'s ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', originally published in [[1989]].<ref name="gg4">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref>

Burger continued to build upon established elements in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], including mentions of the [[Ghhhk/Legends|Ghhhk]] from<ref name="blog" /> [[1977]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']],<ref name="anh">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="ccg">{{CCG|set=A New Hope Limited|cardname=Ghhhk}}</ref> and the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]<ref name="blog" /> from [[R. A. Salvatore]]'s [[1999]] novel [[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime|''Vector Prime'']], published as part of [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''The New Jedi Order'']] series.<ref name="vp">''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime]]''</ref> While the mention of the Ghhhk was cut from the final entry, the Yuuzhan Vong War reference was kept. Burger's intentions in mentioning the war had been to tie the Y'bith into the modern Expanded Universe. When describing the physical traits of the Y'bith, Burger wanted the mutations to be both a blessing and a curse to the species, giving them positive and negative traits.<ref name="blog" />

In order to further differentiate the Y'bith from the Bith, Burger wrote them as violent and temperamental beings, far removed from what he perceived as pacifist tendencies in the Bith. He made even more ties to the Expanded Universe with his mentions of Clak'dor IV,<ref name="blog" /> originally mentioned in the [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]] ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron]]''{{'s}} [[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 17|seventeenth issue]],<ref name="xw17">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 17|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 17]]</ref> published [[April 2]], [[1997]],<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54662/star_wars_x-wing_rogue_squadron_1995_17|text=Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron (1995) #17}}</ref> and Nar Shaddaa, from the ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]'' comic series' [[Dark Empire 3|third issue]],<ref name="de3">[[Dark Empire 3|''Dark Empire'' 3]]</ref> published [[April 21]], [[1992]].<ref name="Marvel DE">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54059/star_wars_dark_empire_1991_3|text=Star Wars: Dark Empire (1991) #3}}</ref> Burger originally named the capital of Clak'dor IV "Nozho II,"<ref name="blog" /> in reference to Nozho from ''Galaxy Guide 4''.<ref name="gg4" /> The name was later changed to "New Nozho" by StarWars.com staff.<ref name="blog" />
